### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e60349970ea504585179cb9a66b9ea344d627c46` — the merge of head `880ca983a72fc3e461c7482c971b66d0c4e20c14` into base `45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e60349970ea504585179cb9a66b9ea344d627c46 && git checkout e60349970ea504585179cb9a66b9ea344d627c46
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 880ca983a72fc3e461c7482c971b66d0c4e20c14 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 && git merge --no-ff 880ca983a72fc3e461c7482c971b66d0c4e20c14

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `880ca983a72fc3e461c7482c971b66d0c4e20c14`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **Face:** the declaration only. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on the PR body and the changeset; the widening is the newly exported lint rule id `SECURITY_CBP_MASTER_REFERENCE_HIDDEN`. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` source and no governed path, and declares no narrowing.
- **The gate's verdict is unchanged.** `assertControlledByParentWrite` now wraps the old body, renamed `judgeControlledByParentWrite`. It rewrites only a refusal the gate itself raised (one `MASTER_EDIT_DENIAL_LEG` names) and keeps the leg on the new error. Every other error passes through as raised.
- **The refusal's words:**
  - A caller who can read the detail's master reference keeps the specific sentence, word for word.
  - A caller who cannot read it gets the same `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with a rule-level sentence. It names no master object, no master record and no leg, and its details are `{ operation, object }` only.
  - "Can read" is the plugin's own readable projection (`getReadableFields`), the one the data plane's reads mask by. It is read for the request's context, so a delegated write intersects the delegator's mask.
  - It fails closed: a throw, an unresolvable answer or no relation all take the generic sentence.
- **Coverage:** every refusal the gate builds, on update, delete and create: the master's object permission, row-level security, record sharing, a master further up the chain, and the owner rule of a row whose optional master is empty.
- **The lint warning** `security-controlled-by-parent-master-reference-hidden`:
  - It reuses the existing controlled-by-parent recogniser; `resolveCbpRelation` now also records the field.
  - It is not reported where View All or Modify All on the detail makes the mask inert.
  - It has an `os explain` entry.
  - The census found 0 hits across first-party apps, examples and templates.

### ② Semver level

Patch for `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/lint`.
- The refusal-text change keeps status, code, accepted input and success answers. This follows the plugin-security refusal-wording precedents, which declared no narrowing.
- The new warning follows the `30804` lint precedent. It states that `os lint --strict` and `os validate --strict` fail on any warning.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No open question.
- Residuals the dev reported, carried by the seat and not blocking this PR:
  - a 422 on a stored row whose required master reference is empty, which names that field;
  - whether self-explain of a write, or the attachment hooks, carry the leg for a caller who cannot read the reference. This is not measured.

  Both go to the seat's follow-up list.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-6pr9`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
